newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX heating oil sends oil complex to lower end.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX heating oil sends oil complex to lower end.

text.p: The NYMEX oil complex ended lower Thursday after warmer-than-expected forecasts for the U.S. Northeast pushed down heating oil in thin trade.

"Heating oil pushed everything lower. If it weren't for heat, we may have gained today," said Dimon Oil trader Herbert Harris. Volume was thin as many dealers extended their Christmas holiday through the end of the week.
January heating oil ended 1.34 cents a gallon lower at 70.06 cents while January gasoline ended off 0.05 cent a gallon at 69.51 cents. February crude ended 18 cents a barrel lower at $24.92.
"It was all due to the warmer forecasts," said a dealer, explaining heating oil's fall.
The National Weather Service's six to 10 day forecast called for normal temperatures in the key heating oil market of the northeastern United States when dealers had expected a colder forecast.
Moreover, Weather Services Corp forecasted above average temperatures through the weekend in the Northeast.
Gasoline's losses were limited on talk of a catalytic cracker at Tosco's Bayway refinery in New Jersey being shut for maintenance turnaround. Tosco declined comment.
The 140,000 barrel per day gasoline making unit has not regained full operating capacity after a fire shut it down two and a half weeks ago.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk ((212-859-1761))
